name: SE Route

pitch_detail.notes: Broad gully; stay center/right for the easiest class-2 line
The gully tops out around 8,150 ft; the 8,514 ft summit is roughly 360 ft above

descent_text: Reverse the ascent. Downclimb the SE gully, mostly class 2-3, staying in the main gully rather than drifting left onto harder ground, which is easy to do in fog. At the foot of the gullies a snowfield leads down; early in the season it is firm in the morning and may call for crampons, and by afternoon it softens enough to boot-ski or plunge-step. Below it, the burned hillside of ash and deadfall is the slowest part going up but quick coming down by plunge-stepping, and it leads back to the old logging road and the Eightmile Trail. No rappels are needed.
approach: Leave the Eightmile Trail onto an old logging road, then boot up an ashen, deadfall-choked burn-zone hillside for about 1,000 ft of gain. Above the burn, continue cross-country up and left toward the SE gullies, crossing a snowfield before reaching the base of the S/SE gully; expect some brief bushwhacking, loose steep dirt, and side-hilling/boulder-hopping en route.
overview: A faster alternative to the standard West Ridge: leaves the Eightmile Trail early to go cross-country up Cashmere's southeast slopes, roughly halving the round-trip mileage before finishing up a broad gully between the south and southeast ridges.
beta: From the Eightmile Trail, cut cross-country up through an old burn zone, then continue up and left toward the gully between the S and SE ridges. The S/SE gully is wide and offers a 'choose your own adventure' character: the center/right line is mostly class 2, while the climbers-left side holds solid class 3-4 rock. The gully tops out at roughly 8,150 ft, about 360 vertical feet below the 8,501 ft top. This line cuts the standard 8-9 mile one-way West Ridge approach roughly in half.
